optimizedDescription.value: Runs trusted graph-index tasks in a lock-owning child process with validated IPC, typed failures, signal forwarding, and complete cleanup.

optimizedContext.value:
# Isolated Index Worker

## Rules

- `@specd/code-graph` public entrypoint SHALL expose `runIsolatedGraphIndex` plus host-facing input, progress, result, typed-error contracts. Input MUST contain graph storage root, trusted installed task-module URL/absolute path, JSON-serializable task input; MAY contain progress callback. Resolve task result after successful terminal child message. MUST NOT call `process.exit()`, render output, interpret CLI formats, or mutate host-global exit state.
- Acquire shared graph index lock for storage root before child creation. Concurrent same-root run MUST fail with typed busy error before second fork. Supervisor owns lock through full child lifetime; releases exactly once after every terminal path: success, task failure, startup/send/IPC failure, invalid/duplicate terminal IPC, premature/non-zero exit, signal, native crash.
- Startup, IPC setup, or initial `send` failure MUST terminate boundedly even without `exit`: detach listeners, tear down IPC, release lease exactly once, settle typed startup failure after best-effort child termination. Lock acquisition/release/path and unlocked assertions remain internal; callers MUST NOT manage lock tokens.
- Production SHALL use `node:child_process.fork` with dedicated worker entrypoint from same installed `@specd/code-graph`. Child contains task execution, parsers, provider native code, synchronous graph-store work; native crash MUST NOT terminate host.
- After successful terminal result, child SHALL finish task resource cleanup and exit code 0. Crash/signal after apparent result remains abnormal. Cleanup MUST address lifecycle faults; MUST NOT use `process.exit()` as mask. Production MUST NOT offer worker-thread/in-process isolation; tests MAY inject launcher or use dedicated protocol seam.
- Worker SHALL dynamically load exactly host-supplied task-module URL/absolute path exposing documented async graph-index entrypoint. Entrypoint receives task input plus JSON-serializable progress emitter; returns one JSON-serializable result or throws one failure. Missing/non-callable entrypoint or non-serializable input/progress/result MUST become typed task/protocol failure.
- Task selection MUST NOT be end-user CLI argument. Host selects trusted, installed, version-affine module; capability is not untrusted-code sandbox.
- Parent/child SHALL use tagged, runtime-validated IPC distinguishing progress, successful terminal result, task-reported terminal failure, malformed/unsupported messages, termination without valid terminal message. Accept at most one terminal message. Duplicate/late terminal message SHALL be protocol failure; MUST NOT cause second settlement, signal action, or lock release.
- Raw IPC envelopes/bootstrap commands remain internal. Public surface MAY expose presentation-neutral progress/failure values; hosts MUST NOT send/parse/validate child messages.
- Forward valid progress values to optional callback in arrival order, without rendering/lossy transformation. Missing callback MUST NOT alter execution. Child/supervisor MUST NOT emit normal progress/result in CLI text, JSON, or TOON; hosts own presentation.
- Preserve distinct typed failures for busy lock; fork/IPC startup; invalid task module/contract; task failure; malformed/unsupported/late/duplicate IPC; non-zero/premature exit; signal termination. Errors MUST extend `SpecdCodeGraphError`, expose stable upper-snake-case codes, actionable messages, structured exit-code/signal details where applicable. Hosts MUST NOT parse stderr/message text for classification.
- During active child, install parent `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` handlers forwarding same signal; remove only installed handlers after termination. Then wait for child, release lock, report typed signal-derived failure. MUST NOT exit/re-signal host.
- Child SHALL receive internal code-graph indication that supervisor owns shared lock; child provider indexing MUST avoid reacquisition. Indication MUST NOT be caller-managed/public, MUST stay forked-child scoped, MUST NOT disable locking for unrelated process/storage root.
- Build SHALL emit stable ESM child entrypoint under published `dist/`. `runIsolatedGraphIndex` SHALL resolve relative to installed module, not repository root, current working directory, or TypeScript source. Package verification MUST fork emitted worker from built/publish-shaped output and dynamically import built task module. Built integration verification MUST force project index, receive terminal result, complete cleanup, exit code 0.
- Listener removal, child-reference cleanup, IPC teardown, lock release SHALL be idempotent and complete before returned promise settles. Remove no foreign listener; leave no lock file, live child, or open IPC channel.

## Constraints

- Only child process satisfies native-crash containment.
- MUST NOT implement queueing, lock waiting, automatic retry, stale-lock PID recovery, scheduled indexing, or background indexing.
- MUST NOT depend on `@specd/sdk`, `@specd/cli`, Commander, or delivery formatter.
- Inputs, progress, results, IPC payloads MUST be JSON-serializable and runtime-validated at process boundary.
- Direct lock helpers and raw IPC DTOs remain internal.
